title: Facial Scrubber
description: A facial scrubber that started from a diagnosis of Dove's scrubber and others like it: the grips weren't made to be held at the angles our faces need, and neither were the round pads. Taking the peacock as inspiration, the shapes in its feathers became both the pad and the grip, around a spherical, tapered body that can be twisted and turned while still holding firm.

brief.label: Objective
brief.text: Diagnose the issues in an existing product, then bring an abstracted feature from an animal into it in an innovative way.

brief.label: Design response
brief.text: A spherical shape with a tapered grip that's easy to twist or turn yet stays gripped, since the motor vibrates. Pads take their shape from peacock feathers.

brief.label: Key features
brief.text: Ergonomic, non-slip grip. Magnetic interchangeable pads. USB-C universal plug and quick charging.

brief.label: Materials
brief.text: The body is casein-clay-glyceraldehyde plastic, made from milk protein, clay and a reactive molecule: strong, water-resistant and sustainable. Three curved sections make it easy to injection mold and assemble, and the flat base keeps the pad off the sink. Packaging is EPS: 100% recyclable, 98% air, compression-resistant and moldable into almost any shape.

brief.label: Process
brief.text: Natural-form ideation, then rounds of ergonomic studies in the hand, then a final visualization.

study_intro: Biomimicry as a starting point: the peacock's feather shapes, abstracted until they become a grip and a pad.

study.label: Form
study.text: A sphere tapering into a grip, so it can be rolled and turned in the fingers at the angles a face needs.

study.label: Reference
study.text: The curve and eye of a peacock feather, reinterpreted twice: once in the pad outline and once in the hand-hold.

study.label: Color
study.text: Gloss white with a single band of red marking the seam between body and cap: clinical, with one warm accent.

study.label: Detail
study.text: A flat base so it sits upright and keeps the pad off the counter between uses.
